target_customer: Busy, cost conscious and tech minded consumers wanting a complete nutrition meal replacement, later mainstream retail shoppers
problem: Cooking and buying food was time consuming and expensive; Soylent offered all essential nutrients in a cheap, simple powder or drink.
business_model: Consumer packaged goods sold direct by subscription and later through retailers such as Amazon, Walmart and Kroger

founders.name: John Coogan
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as an entrepreneur in consumer packaged goods technology based in Los Angeles.

founders.name: Hunter Scott
founders.background_notes: YC page: hardware engineer with more than ten years of experience.

founders.name: Matt Cauble
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page, no bio.

founders.name: Kumar T
founders.background_notes: YC page: small business owner and angel investor.

technical_complexity.rationale: Formulating a nutritionally complete product and manufacturing it at food grade scale needed nutrition science and supply chain work; later recalls in 2016 show scaling quality issues.

defensibility.rationale: The formula was open source early on and copycats such as Huel launched in 2015 and became larger competitors per Sacra.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought Soylent early; Starco Brands bought it in February 2023.

market_need_then: The founder's blog post and 2013 crowdfunding drew strong consumer interest; the 3 million dollar crowdfunding figure comes from a search snippet and is unverified.

branding.name_origin: Chosen from the novel Make Room Make Room or the film Soylent Green, per press; sources disagree, and Wikipedia derived text says the morbid association was chosen to pique curiosity.

identity.visual_style: Minimal packaging; green label redesign around 2018 to 2019
identity.voice_and_tone: Self aware humor; 2019 campaign Soylent is plants not people leaned into Soylent Green jokes

branding.brand_signature: The Soylent Green name and joke, embraced in a 2019 Mint Chocolate campaign
branding.community_and_virality: The name is a meme per Know Your Meme and drew heavy press; the 2019 spoof campaign made the joke official.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable, widely covered name that drove awareness and curiosity, but the dystopian connotation was a recurring joke and a brand risk.

outcome_analysis: Soylent became one of the best known YC consumer brands after 2013, raising a 20 million Series A in January 2015 at an estimated 100 million valuation and a 50 million Series B in May 2017, for about 71 to 75 million total per aggregators. It was sold to Starco Brands in February 2023 for 29.4 million, well below funds raised, after 2016 recalls and rivals like Huel growing faster per Sacra. Starco holds the brand and the site stays live.
notes: Competitor search returned only later rivals (Huel 2015, Sated, Vade) so the competitor list is empty; no dated 2012 to 2013 competitor source found. Total raised ranges 71.5M to 74.5M by source. A 2015 estimated valuation of about 100 million is reported by AgFunder but not stated as post money, so post_money_usd is null. Seed amount of 1.5M and date come from AgFunder quoting Recode; date not stated. The crowdfunding 3M is an unverified snippet. Exit amount 29.4M per MarketScreener and TechCrunch coverage; one source describes it as a merger. 2016 recalls are mentioned in the Bloomberg headline only. The scaling_failed failure factor is a loose fit and low confidence. success_factors is a judgment.
